avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide causes potassium depletion; concurrent supplementation may lead to hypokalemia if patient is already depleted, though some patients may need supplementation based on individual monitoring
avoid_supplements.action: Only use potassium supplements under direct physician supervision with regular serum potassium monitoring

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice root
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention and potassium loss, compounding hydrochlorothiazide's electrolyte-depleting effects and increasing hypokalemia and hypertension risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid licorice root supplements entirely; monitor for signs of hypokalemia (muscle weakness, palpitations)

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild hypertensive effects, potentially counteracting antihypertensive benefits of hydrochlorothiazide
caution_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor blood pressure regularly and discuss with healthcare provider

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide may reduce urinary calcium excretion, increasing serum calcium levels when combined with supplementation
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum calcium levels periodically; adjust supplementation dose as needed based on lab values

avoid_foods.name: Excessive sodium/salt
avoid_foods.mechanism: High sodium intake counteracts the diuretic and antihypertensive effects of hydrochlorothiazide, reducing efficacy
avoid_foods.action: Maintain sodium restriction (<2300 mg/day as recommended); counsel patient on reading food labels and avoiding processed foods

caution_foods.name: Potassium-rich foods (bananas, spinach, sweet potatoes)
caution_foods.mechanism: While hydrochlorothiazide depletes potassium, moderate intake of potassium-rich foods may help maintain balance depending on individual serum levels
caution_foods.action: Consume in moderation; base intake on serum potassium levels and physician recommendation; some patients may benefit while others require restriction

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods and beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine has mild diuretic and hypertensive effects that may slightly amplify hydrochlorothiazide's effects
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake to moderate levels (<200 mg/day); monitor blood pressure response

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum electrolytes (especially potassium, sodium, calcium), glucose, lipid panel, and uric acid regularly as hydrochlorothiazide can affect these parameters. Assess blood pressure control and counsel on sodium restriction as the primary dietary intervention for optimizing efficacy.
